newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call closes lower, securities on bull run.
newsitem.headline: Indian call closes lower, securities on bull run.

text.p: Indian call money rates closed lower at 1.00-1.50 percent, against the day's opening levels of 1.50-2.00 percent, dealers said.
"Most of the deals were at 1.50-1.75 percent levels with some stray deals at 1.0 percent," one dealer said.
The rates are expected to rule below 2.50 percent for the rest of the fortnight, while the next fortnight will see some firmness on new issue auction, he added.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) will auction six-year paper for 30 billion rupees on July 16.
The issue will have a cut-off in the region of 11.95-12.05 percent, a primary dealer said. "Foreign banks and private banks will try to quote below 11.95 percent to bring down the yield," he said.
But the maximum bids will be seen above the 11.95 percent levels, he added.
The securities market continued its bull run on Tuesday while volumes were steady at 5.40 billion rupees on the National Stock Exchange (NSE), an NSE dealer said.
Securities' prices rose in the morning session and fell on profit taking by banks at mid-session, to rebound near the close on fresh investments, a dealer said.
The 12.59 percent government stock 2004 attracted more buyers with a volume of 1.62 billion rupees, he said.
The price ranged from 102.43 to 102.55 rupees, against the previous close of 102.29 rupees, he added.
Yield on treasury bills maturing in April 98 was unchanged at 7.90 percent, a dealer said.
The IFCI certificate of deposit maturing in June 98 was traded at 10 percent levels, a dealer said.
